no_deviation_areas: the capability key set, the three-valued presence enum, the unknown-is-absent rule, the ordinary-hosting profile and the four operations follow the freeze exactly
no table, no migration, no HTTP surface
no change to any package other than larena/core

B.detail: The first rule reported any difference between a declared and a detected presence value. Wiring the profile into the doctor produced ten findings on an ordinary development machine, five of them 'declared absent, detected unknown' — not a disagreement, because both mean the capability is not there.
B.resolution: A mismatch is a difference in availability. The raw difference stays readable through differs(). The same machine now reports five findings, every one a real difference. Ten findings is how an operator learns to ignore the environment section, which is worse than having none.
B.found_by: running larena:doctor, not by reading the code
B.shape_impact: none on the frozen profile document; the diagnostic gains one method

B.detail: PHPStan objected that five default probes declared ?bool and always return bool.
B.resolution: Those five declare bool; the storage-path probe keeps ?bool because it genuinely cannot answer without a path. The array's type still allows either, because 'I could not tell' has to be expressible.

B.detail: core.environment.declare validates a profile document and returns it with its fingerprint; it does not store it.
B.resolution: Where a declaration lives is an application concern and core owns no table for it, which is also why this batch adds no migration. Recorded so a later batch knows the persistence decision is still open.

C.detail: The freeze lists four topology reason codes, none of which covers a node whose requirement the host does not meet — yet the freeze also requires that case to be refused naming the capability.
C.resolution: Added environment_requirement_unmet alongside them, with the missing capabilities listed separately so a reader sees which one. Recorded as an amendment on the launch record.
C.shape_impact: one reason code added to the topology report; nothing removed or renamed

C.detail: The freeze distinguishes 'more than one node' from 'a cluster' without saying where the line is.
C.resolution: More than two nodes is a cluster. A pair is the ordinary web-and-worker split and needs remote operations; three or more is a topology somebody has to operate, which is what the cluster capability is for. Stated in isCluster() and in the document.
C.shape_impact: none on the manifest; one rule now explicit

C.detail: Conflict detection needs to know what is already installed, and there is no installed-solution registry in this batch.
C.resolution: The planner takes a map keyed by solution id. No new contract, and no table: this batch plans and nothing owns an installed set yet.

C.detail: Five new operations invalidate the asserted core operation count in two package tests and one root composition test.
C.resolution: 26 became 31 in all three. The counts are asserted rather than derived on purpose — an operation appearing without anyone noticing is what they are for.
